problem: A durable fleet execution-continuity artifact declared BLOCKED but its terminal_state.blocker code/evidence did not match the embedded blocker_proof, so execution_continuity.py would reject the claimed terminal boundary despite the prose appearing plausible.

hypotheses.statement: CDC lacked a rule binding BLOCKED terminal_state to blocker_proof.
The continuity artifact failed because no fresh blocker proof existed.
hypotheses.observed_result: A blocker_proof existed, but terminal_state.blocker carried a different code and different evidence refs.

hypotheses.statement: The durable continuity payload was assembled from human-readable status facts without running the released execution_continuity validator before persistence.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare coupled fields inside the stored artifact against the validator contract and rebuild them from one proof object.
hypotheses.observed_result: The stored artifact had internally inconsistent coupled fields; rebuilding terminal_state.blocker directly from the single blocker_proof produced an exact binding.

correction: Construct terminal continuity artifacts from one schema-typed blocker proof object and run the released execution_continuity/Terminal-State v2 checks before durable write. Coupled code/evidence/next-action/recheck-trigger fields must be generated from the same source object, not independently copied from prose/status summaries.
defense_in_depth: Retain a regression case where blocker_proof and terminal_state.blocker differ by code or evidence and require persistence/finalization to fail closed; dogfood control-plane writers must validate their artifact before commit.
invariant: Every durable BLOCKED continuity artifact is schema-valid and internally bound at commit time: terminal_state.blocker exactly matches blocker_proof, and no unvalidated free-form terminal payload is persisted.
